messages:
maria: Hey team, hitting a reproducible issue in the Kotlin sample: when network comes back WorkManager fires a bunch of small upload jobs, OkHttp ends up running ~16 concurrent calls and our auth refresh runs for each one. Getting 401/429 cascade.

aj: Ouch. Do we do singleflight refresh anywhere in the sample interceptor?

maria: No, current AuthInterceptor just checks expiry and calls tokenProvider.refresh() inline.

sophia: Thats the classic stampede. Two options: implement a singleflight (Deferred/Mutex) or centralize uploads behind an AggregatorWorker that drains a queue.

tim: Also check OkHttp client config in sample. If retryOnConnectionFailure=true and Dispatcher maxRequestsPerHost is high, you can magnify bursts when connectivity returns.

maria: Client snippet from sample:

```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 64; maxRequestsPerHost = 20 })
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor(tokenProvider))
  .build()
```

maria: Logs when network flips (trim):

```
2026-02-27 08:01:11 UploadWorker: network available, start batch 0..15
2026-02-27 08:01:11 AuthInterceptor: token expired -> refresh start
2026-02-27 08:01:11 AuthInterceptor: token expired -> refresh start
2026-02-27 08:01:12 Retrofit: 401 Unauthorized
2026-02-27 08:01:12 Retrofit: 429 Too Many Requests
```

aj: Two immediate mitigations: lower maxRequestsPerHost to ~4, and make token refresh singleflight. For coroutines, use an AtomicReference<Deferred<Token>> or a Mutex with a cached deferred so other callers await it rather than running their own refresh.

sophia: Example singleflight using AtomicReference<Deferred> pattern (suspend-friendly):

```kotlin
private val refreshRef = AtomicReference<Deferred<Token>?>(null)
private suspend fun singleflightRefresh(): Token {
  val ongoing = refreshRef.get()
  if (ongoing != null) return ongoing.await()
  val newDeferred = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO).async(start = CoroutineStart.LAZY) { tokenProvider.refresh() }
  if (!refreshRef.compareAndSet(null, newDeferred)) return refreshRef.get()!!.await()
  try {
    newDeferred.start()
    return newDeferred.await()
  } finally {
    refreshRef.set(null)
  }
}
```

tim: Good pattern. Also ensure worker cancellation cancels Retrofit/OkHttp calls. Our coroutine CallAdapter must call call.cancel() when the coroutine is cancelled; otherwise you get lingering inflight requests. We had a bug in an older adapter where cancellations were ignored.

maria: Sophia, could we add an AggregatorWorker template to the sample that uses ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP and a single bounded queue so uploads don't duplicate?

sophia: Yep. Happy to open PR: will (1) add AggregatorWorker, (2) reduce dispatcher concurrency defaults, (3) swap AuthInterceptor to singleflight Deferred, (4) add integration test for offline->online ensuring only 1 refresh call.

aj: Suggest also making retryOnConnectionFailure=false in the sample. Leave a short note in README about adapter cancellation semantics and WorkManager behavior (backoff vs queued work).

ci-bot: CI: PR 4567 queued for sampleapp - tests: emulator-pixel6, rosetta, integration.

maria: Awesome. I'll validate on Pixel 8 and on a slow 3G emulator. If anyone can smoke test wifi->mobile toggles, ping me.

sophia: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/sampleapp/pull/4567 :sparkles: includes test and docs.

aj: I'll add a tiny instrumentation test to assert dispatcher.queuedCalls doesn't exceed 4 in the aggregation case.

maria: Thanks all  will report results after verifying. :thumbsup:
